stem: What weekly intake of carbonated drinks is associated with high erosion risk in children, according to risk prediction guidance?
options: More than two
More than six
More than 14
More than 21
justification: The text states that intake of more than 14 carbonated drinks weekly is associated with high erosion risk, while more than six is associated with moderate erosion risk.

stem: In dentists delivering sedation to children, what type of course completion is required as documented evidence of competency?
options: A theoretical training course covering the principles of sedation practice
A course in advanced orthodontic mechanics
A certification in general anaesthesia administration only
A course exclusively in pharmacology of local anaesthetics
justification: The text specifies satisfactory completion of a theoretical training course covering the principles of sedation practice as part of documented evidence of competency for dentists delivering sedation.

stem: According to dental caries epidemiology trends, what has happened to caries experience in the primary dentition since about 1986-1987, in contrast to the permanent dentition?
options: It has continued to decline at the same rate
It may have stabilized, while permanent dentition caries prevalence and severity continued to decline
It has increased dramatically worldwide
It has been eradicated entirely in developed nations
justification: The text notes that caries prevalence and severity in the permanent dentition have continued to decline since 1982 in Canada and the USA, but that caries experience in the primary dentition may have stabilized since about 1986-1987.

stem: What is emphasized as the best overall approach to tackling the problem of dental caries in children, according to the introduction on operative treatment?
options: Immediate extraction of all carious primary teeth
An effective programme of prevention
Routine placement of stainless steel crowns on all molars
Delaying treatment until the permanent dentition erupts
justification: The text states there is no doubt that the best way to tackle the problem of dental caries is through an effective programme of prevention, as outlined in previous chapters.

stem: Regarding remineralization of early smooth surface lesions in the young permanent dentition, which key point is emphasized?
options: Early smooth surface lesions are reversible
The surface layer of enamel contains most fluoride and is most resistant to caries
Restorations should always be replaced rather than repaired
Fluoride has no effect on enamel remineralization
justification: The key points state that the surface layer of enamel contains most fluoride and is most resistant to caries, which is central to the remineralization discussion.

stem: In the internal bleaching technique described for advanced restorative dentistry, what concentration of hydrogen peroxide is used along with a heating light with rheostat?
justification: The armamentarium lists 30-35% hydrogen peroxide alongside a heating light with rheostat as part of the internal bleaching technique.

stem: When should toothbrushing begin, according to guidance on home-based oral health care for children?
options: Only after all primary teeth have erupted
As soon as the first primary tooth erupts
At the age of two years
When the first permanent molar erupts
justification: The text states that toothbrushing should start as soon as the first primary tooth erupts, and it is recommended that teeth are brushed twice daily.

stem: In the recommended protocol for regenerative endodontic treatment, what concentration of sodium hypochlorite is used for irrigation during the first treatment visit?
options: 0.5% NaOCl
1.5% NaOCl
5.25% NaOCl
10% NaOCl
justification: The protocol specifies irrigating the root canal system with copious amounts of 1.5% sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) with the needle introduced into the canal.

stem: What long-term benefit is associated with elective loss of severely compromised first permanent molars as part of a comprehensive treatment plan?
options: Guaranteed prevention of future caries in all remaining teeth
The child may benefit from their elective loss as part of a comprehensive treatment plan
Automatic correction of any existing malocclusion without further intervention
Elimination of the need for any future orthodontic assessment
justification: The text states that in the long term the child may benefit from their elective loss of severely compromised first permanent molars as part of a comprehensive treatment plan.

stem: What role might the paediatric dentist provide input on when working closely with an orthodontist in multidisciplinary management?
options: Prognosis of teeth, patient's ability to accept treatment, advanced restorative options, and oral surgery procedures
Selection of orthodontic wire alloy composition exclusively
General anaesthetic dosing for unrelated medical procedures
Design of the practice's radiography suite
justification: The text states such cases may require the paediatric dentist to provide input on a range of issues, including prognosis of teeth, patient's ability to accept treatment, advanced restorative options, and oral surgery procedures.

stem: How does recurrent salivary gland infection typically present over many years in a child, according to the discussion of oral medicine and oral surgery in children?
options: It resolves permanently after a single course of antibiotics
This low-level damage over many years causes increasing permanent damage to the acini and duct structures
It always requires immediate surgical excision of the gland
It has no long-term effect on gland flow rates
justification: The text explains that this low-level damage over many years causes increasing permanent damage to the acini and duct structures, resulting in lower gland flow rates and incomplete emptying of the ductal system.

stem: Why are general anaesthetics considered a particular problem for children with adrenal insufficiency such as Addison's disease?
options: Because of the pre-anaesthetic fasting that is required, so these are normally carried out on an inpatient basis
Because general anaesthesia is contraindicated in all endocrine disorders
Because adrenal insufficiency causes resistance to anaesthetic agents
Because these children cannot receive any form of sedation
justification: The text explains that general anaesthetics are a problem because of the pre-anaesthetic fasting that is required, and so these are normally carried out on an inpatient basis to enable the insulin and carbohydrate balance to be stabilized intravenously.

stem: In the history of accidental injuries in children, which characteristic distinguishes them from suspicious injuries?
options: Accidental injuries typically involve bony prominences and match the history and developmental stage of the child
Accidental injuries always involve soft tissue areas like the ears and neck
Accidental injuries occur exclusively at night
Accidental injuries never involve the head or face
justification: The text notes that accidental injuries typically involve bony prominences, match the history, and are in keeping with the development of the child, listing sites such as elbows, knees, shins, and forehead.

stem: According to research on needle phobia and dental anxiety in children, what is the reported prevalence of needle phobia in 4- to 6-year-olds?
options: As high as 5%
As high as 19%
As high as 40%
As high as 60%
justification: The text cites that Montiero et al. (2014) indicate that the prevalence of needle phobia may be as high as 19% in 4- to 6-year-olds.

stem: What is the key to successful management of molar incisor hypomineralization (MIH)?
options: Immediate extraction of all affected teeth
Early identification, with careful review around the time of eruption of the first permanent molars
Delaying any preventive intervention until adulthood
Applying orthodontic brackets to affected teeth immediately
justification: The text states that the key to successful management of this condition is early identification, with careful review needed around the time of eruption of the first permanent molars to identify affected teeth.
